rationale: Both parse and validate identically, return defensive copies from Rows and Cols, and bounds-check Set. A keeps the stub's design: Matrix is simply [][]int with value-receiver methods, which is minimal and fits Go well. B adds an exported Matrix interface plus an unexported concrete struct that caches a column count. That is extra abstraction the task does not need, and returning an interface from a constructor goes against the common Go guidance to return concrete types. B's caching of the column count is tidy, but it does not justify the added indirection. A achieves the same robustness with less machinery, so it is the cleaner solution.
